standing: Author correction for review finding PS-01, revision 5. Proposed minimal successor delta to the security S9 owner plus its private lifecycle companion. Not an accepted amendment, not executable product code, not a wire schema and not acceptance of frozen candidate25 bytes. Requires its own substantive review on newly frozen bytes.

revision.supersedes: claude-planning-owner-correction.v4 store-instance-lineage.v1.json (sha256 a8ee21b307b6ccc1...), superseding v3 (170ec81d5d3ad1d4...), v2 (7565223e825ebcfe...) and v1 (4dd6291fbf526010...)
v4ToV5Changes: Marker availability is now PHASE-SENSITIVE, bound to the owner own decision. A forward selection target store does not exist at LEASED or PREPARING and may already be reclaimed at ABORTED; v4 required selectedStoreRoot in every branch and turned the owner lawful early ABORT into a quarantine. Only a settled transition requires the target marker.

The target observation is a closed three-way outcome: readable, absent (not materialised yet or reclaimed) and unreadable (observed but not admissible). An unreadable target never becomes an absent one, and an absence must be stated explicitly rather than inferred from a missing key.

admit_node now validates chain and uniqueness on the IDEMPOTENT path as well. v4 returned idempotent on an exact key match before checking ancestry, so an existing target whose chain was broken validated with no refusal. The idempotent path still writes nothing and rewrites no origin.

The single-lineage-root rule is scoped to the COMPONENT reachable from the node under consideration, not globally. An authorized restore or adoption starts its own lineage, so several roots may coexist across unrelated stores.

Node shape is admitted by the REAL closed schema through the frozen foundation ExactValidator, whose integer type checker refuses a JSON boolean. The law no longer assumes member sets, types or version constants; a caller that has already admitted its inputs must say so with an explicit labelled assumption, and otherwise the law refuses rather than guessing.
v3ToV4Changes: Node identity at every decision point is now the FULL TRIPLE, whose instance component is read from the store-root MARKER of the store the transition actually selects. v3 searched by the numeric (storeGeneration, stateSchema) pair, so a retained old branch at (b,4,2) blocked a fresh target at (e,4,2); root executed the actual owner-admitted intentStoreMigrate and v3 wrongly quarantined against owner ABORT at LEASED and owner RESUME-COMMIT at COMMITTED. Accepted as a real defect.
intentDigest is never a global search key. The record schema already says it may repeat, so it is validated ON the selected node and never scanned for across the node set.

One admission law, admit_node, is now applied by BOTH publication and recovery, on the decision path. v3 reconstructed a forward node without checking that its predecessor existed and wrote broken ancestry with refusal None; the whole-set invariants helper detected it but was never consulted at the boundary.
A duplicate exact primary key whose contents disagree refuses instead of selecting the first match.
Markers are validated for presence and shape before any dereference.
BUSY, REFUSE and QUARANTINE now make NO companion decision at all and inspect no node, matching the prose. v3 prose said so but the generic non-settled branch still inspected nodes.
The ancestor re-selection join uses the retained selected marker and the verified chain from the current node, never a global numeric match.
correctionOf remedy metadata corrected: the owner patch is two hunks and its current filename is security-and-lifecycle.md.S9-pair-law-and-S9.3.patch.
v2ToV3Changes: Recovery is now CONDITIONAL on the same selection case as publication. v2's durabilityAndReconciliation, recoveryTotality and S9.3 reconstructed a node unconditionally on COMMITTED/DONE; root executed the v2 reconstruct() against the owner-admitted frozen intentRepair and it produced a node whose predecessor equalled its own triple. Accepted as a real defect; see rootCounterexamples.

The selection case is now a pure function of the admitted intent, never of the stored node set. An earlier draft of this revision asked whether the to pair appeared in the stored ancestry, which let a damaged lineage reclassify a rollback as a forward selection and fabricate a node; that draft failure is retained in the control history.

The claim that S9.2 publishes no core-rollback store rule is WITHDRAWN. The published reference admit_transition_intent enforces the schema/store pair for core-update and core-rollback alike, and the S9 footprint already owns reselect. A minimal prose statement of that pair law is added to S9.2 itself so a blind consumer need not consult an excluded model.

v2's node-writing matrix labelled (5,1)->(4,1) a schema retreat for both rollback kinds. The owner refuses both. All cases are now owner-admitted eleven-member intents drawn from the frozen fixtures, with one composed schema-retreating core-rollback admitted before use.

The lineage root law is generalised from installation only to any authorized local act that materialises a new physical store, so an evidence restore or portable adoption has a lawful root without inventing a public transition.
The canonical digest recipe no longer says a raw digest cannot collide with the framed identity; it states representation and domain separation plus the standard collision-resistance assumption.
v1ToV2Changes: Record redesigned from a per-transition attempt row to a per-binding-triple LINEAGE NODE, keyed by the triple, written only after the journal record is durably COMMITTED. This removes the intentDigest primary-key contradiction on lawful retry (issue 7), removes the S9.3-5/S9.3-8 rewrite-versus-discard contradiction (issue 5), and makes the rollback and schema-preserving cases fall out of the data instead of the operation name (issue 6).
Node-writing is derived from the admitted intent's own from/to values, because S9.2 does not publish a store-generation rule for core-rollback (issue 6).
Recovery is now total over all six InstallationTransitionJournalV1 states and never replaces an owner ABORT with a quarantine (issue 5).
Cross-file atomicity is no longer claimed. The node is derivable from durable owner state, so a one-sided crash footprint reconciles by reconstruction (issue 7).

canonicalDigestRecipe corrected: the one frozen canonicalizer sorts object members, so input key order does not change the digest (issue 3). The executed control now imports the frozen canonicalizer instead of a stand-in.
Floor and authority behaviour split three ways so an authorized migration's floor carry-forward is not invalidated by the restore rule (issue 4).

correctionOf.withdrawnClaim: S9 validates the exact old/new (storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema) tuple against the transition intent and current registry state.
correctionOf.reason: Verified false against frozen candidate25. The substring storeInstance does not occur anywhere in docs/coop/design-corrections/security/security-lifecycle.schemas.v1.json. InstallationTransitionIntentV1 is additionalProperties:false with exactly 11 properties and InstallationTransitionJournalV1 with exactly 20; neither carries a store instance identity. The S9.2 registry member is $defs/NamespaceList, an array of namespace strings, not a store-instance registry.
correctionOf.remedy: The explicit normative insertion in patches/security-and-lifecycle.md.S9-pair-law-and-S9.3.patch: TWO hunks, both pure insertions with no line removed or altered. Hunk 1 states the schema/store pair law inside S9.2 itself; hunk 2 inserts S9.3 between the end of S9.2 and the S10 heading. No member is added to any closed public or signed record.

frozenSourceAnchors.fact: Closed (additionalProperties:false), exactly 11 required properties: schemaVersion, operation, fromCoreClosure, toCoreClosure, fromStateSchema, toStateSchema, fromStoreGeneration, toStoreGeneration, platformProfileSetBodyDigest, preconditionGeneration, rollbackDeadline. No store instance identity.

Closed, exactly 20 required properties including intentDigest, registry, registryDigest, affects, leaseSet, state, fenceHeld, writtenAfterAllLeasesHeld. No store instance identity. intentDigest is Hex64, described as the raw SHA-256 of the canonical admitted intent and equal to the S15 mutation step inputDescriptorDigest. state is the inline enum LEASED, PREPARING, PREPARED, COMMITTED, DONE, ABORTED.
Array of strings, minLength 1, maxLength 4096, uniqueItems, maxItems 65536, utf8 order. It carries no per-namespace object.

Total over the five operations: core-repair keeps closure, schema and store; core-update changes the closure, never lowers the schema, and selects a new store generation exactly when the schema changes; core-rollback changes the closure, never raises the schema, needs the deadline; store-migrate keeps the core closure, advances the schema and selects a new store generation; store-rollback keeps the core closure, retreats the schema, re-selects the retained generation, needs the deadline.

frozenSourceAnchors.selector: admit_transition_intent, lines 2174-2215, and the TRANSITION_INTENT_KEYS comment at lines 2108-2110
frozenSourceAnchors.fact: The schema/store PAIR LAW is published behavior, not an omission. For BOTH core-update (lines 2189-2192) and core-rollback (lines 2198-2201) the reference refuses TRANSITION.SAME_SCHEMA_KEEPS_STORE when the schema is unchanged and the store generation is not, and TRANSITION.SCHEMA_CHANGE_SELECTS_NEW_STORE when the schema changes and the store generation does not. core-repair must keep closure, schema and store (2177-2183). store-migrate requires an advanced schema and a different generation (2202-2208); store-rollback requires a retreated schema and a different generation (2209-2215). The module's own comment states it directly: a store operation keeps the core closure, a same-schema core operation keeps the store.
frozenSourceAnchors.consequence: Over the admitted space the selection case is decidable from the intent alone: same store with same schema is a same-store selection, an advancing schema is a forward selection, a retreating schema is an ancestor reselect, and no admitted intent changes the store with an unchanged schema.
frozenSourceAnchors.withdrawn: The v2 statement that S9.2 publishes no store-generation rule for core-rollback was an overstatement and is withdrawn. Only the short S9.2 PROSE omits the pair, which is why this correction adds it there.

frozenSourceAnchors.selector: S9 migration footprint and floors, lines 644-657
frozenSourceAnchors.fact: Migration writes a migrating root: PREPARING, PREPARED, old store fenced RESTORED, COMMITTED, final rename. Floors (rootVersion, indexSnapshotVersion, revocationVersion, evalHighWater, lastAccepted, recoveryEpochSerial) COPY FORWARD into the new store; the boot anchor and any pending challenge do not. Rollback inside the 30 d window re-selects the retained old store with floors set to the MAXIMUM of both stores. A poisoned floor is not lowered by migration or rollback; only S4.5 lowers it.

Written under the held fence, only after every lease of the affected set is held, in state LEASED; leaseSet must equal core_transition_affected_namespaces over the registry frozen under the fence. recover_transition_journal is the first act under the next fence, before any project admission, from the durable footprint only. By state: LEASED/PREPARING to ABORT; PREPARED follows the S9 footprint table for a store operation (RESUME-COMMIT from step 3 only when the old store is fenced RESTORED, otherwise ABORT; no footprint to QUARANTINE) while A CORE OPERATION ABORTS because the published generation was never selected and the GC census reclaims it; COMMITTED to RESUME-COMMIT, never reversed; DONE and ABORTED release only. Refusals include CURRENT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH, CURRENT_STORE_MISMATCH and PRECONDITION_GENERATION_MISMATCH.

frozenSourceAnchors.selector: S2 Two canonical profiles, never mixed, lines 90-101
frozenSourceAnchors.fact: Signed security metadata stays under opensip-metadata-canonical.1. Product data, explicitly everything with a schemaVersion, uses the foundation canonicalizer of identity-and-evidence section 3: no normalization, integers to 2^64-1. A decoder for one profile never admits the other's documents.

canonical(value) is json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False, SORT_KEYS=TRUE, separators (',',':'), allow_nan=False, encoded UTF-8, bounded at 4 MiB with depth 32. parse() refuses duplicate keys, floats, non-finite values, negative zero and integers outside -(2**63)..2**64-1. identity(domain, value) is the framed H(domain, descriptor): sha256 over b'opensip.product.v1\0' + domain + b'\0' + 8-byte big-endian length + canonical bytes. A bare sha256 over canonical bytes is therefore demonstrably NOT that framed identity.

frozenSourceAnchors.selector: S1 constants, lines 87-88, and S5 detection bound, lines 306-313
frozenSourceAnchors.fact: No D9 class, code or exit is minted; every refusal maps to an existing D9 v1.14 code. Stated and not detected: a coherent rollback of the entire install root with the marker suppressed.

Named durability boundaries include lifecycle publication. Before visibility there is no partial state. After visibility, FSYNC_FAILED and COMMIT_FAILED leave durability UNDETERMINED: the writer refuses every further effect of the operation, reopens the carrier, reconciles the exact state, and only then decides; it never assumes either the old or the new state.
security v8 5.5 restore keeps floors and provides no floor recovery; retained, with S4 adding the only lawful floor-lowering act. A restore therefore does not lower a floor either.

ownerSuccessorDelta.patchShape: Two hunks, both pure insertions with no line removed or altered, so they three-way merge cleanly with a separate author S1/S6/S9/WA13 edits. Hunk 1 inserts the explicit schema/store pair law into S9.2 itself, which is existing reference behavior rather than a new choice. Hunk 2 inserts S9.3 between the end of S9.2 and the S10 heading.
closedPublicRecordsUnchanged: every opensip-signature-envelope.2 body and the opensip-catalog.1 body
ownerSuccessorDelta.noImpliedWidening: No member is added to any record named above, no signature-envelope kind, no signed document, no public major and no new H-domain. NamespaceList remains an array of strings.
ownerSuccessorDelta.d9Impact: None. Refusals reuse the existing S9.2 TRANSITION.* family under D9 REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED and the existing MIGRATION.CORRUPT quarantine.

privateCompanionSchema.standing: Private local lifecycle record. Never a request, response, wire record, authority token or signed document.

keyModel.whyNotIntentDigest: intentDigest is the raw SHA-256 of an 11-member semantic intent. It is not an attempt identifier. Two lawful situations repeat it: (a) an attempt that aborts before COMMITTED may be retried with a byte-identical intent when preconditionGeneration is unchanged, and (b) a schema-preserving core-repair may be requested twice. A primary key on intentDigest with immutable from/to members would turn a lawful retry into a contradiction. Keying on the admitted binding triple removes the problem without any new public field: a retry that materializes a new store produces a different triple, and a retry that changes nothing produces no node at all.
keyModel.noAttemptDisambiguatorNeeded: No private attempt counter, sequence or occurrence join is introduced. The attempt history that does exist is the owner's own single-slot transition journal footprint (A6), which this companion does not duplicate.

location.instanceMarker: each store's own root, one private regular file, written before that store is first published and never rewritten
location.lineageNodes: the lifecycle transition store owned by crates/lifecycle/src/journal_store.rs, beside the public transition journal
location.notInInventory: Both live inside modules already present in repository-file-inventory.v1.json. This correction adds no inventory row and no generated-section change. The two companion JSON documents are planned architecture sources, not product inventory files.

storeGeneration.description: Held equal to the owner $defs/I64NonNegative. Not monotonic across the lineage: A4 lets a rollback re-select a retained earlier generation.

stateSchema.description: Held equal to the owner $defs/StateSchema enum. The added type keyword narrows, never widens.

predecessor.description: The triple this node was selected from, or null at a lineage root. Always present; an absent member is not a null, mirroring the inherited witness-shape rule in security v8 5.4. A node never names its own triple, and the chain is acyclic.

selectedByIntentDigest.description: The intentDigest of the COMMITTED forward-selection transition that created this node, or null at a lineage root. Evidence, never a key: it may repeat across nodes and across retries. Recovery never writes it onto a node created by an earlier act.

extraAdmissionRules: No unknown member, duplicate JSON key, implicit default or lossy numeric parse. JSON booleans are not integers.
predecessor and selectedByIntentDigest are null together and non-null together. A node with both null is a LINEAGE ROOT; see lineageRoot.
Exactly one lineage root exists per store lineage.
A node predecessor triple must already exist as a node. A node never names its own triple and the chain is acyclic; a self predecessor is a contradiction and quarantines.
Nodes are append-only. A second node with an existing primary key and any differing member is a contradiction and quarantines; a byte-identical re-assertion is idempotent.

Among S9 transitions, only a forward selection creates a node; authorized installation/restore/adoption creates a lineage root under lineageRoot. A node whose selectedByIntentDigest names a same-store or ancestor-reselect transition is a contradiction.
A schema-valid node grants nothing. It records which physical store was selected, never that the store is trusted, readable or authorized.

nodeWritingRule.principle: The selection case is a pure function of the ADMITTED intent and never reads the stored node set. The owner pair law (A4b) makes it decidable: same store with same schema, an advancing schema, or a retreating schema. Deriving it from the intent alone is deliberate, because a case derived from stored ancestry would let a damaged lineage silently reclassify a rollback as a forward selection and fabricate a node.
nodeWritingRule.identicalAtPublicationAndRecovery: Publication and recovery call the same derivation. That is the correction for the v2 defect: v2 published conditionally but reconstructed unconditionally, so an owner-admitted same-store core-repair produced a node whose predecessor was its own triple.

cases.condition: toStoreGeneration equals fromStoreGeneration AND toStateSchema equals fromStateSchema
ownerAdmittedOperations: core-repair (A4b 2177-2183: keeps closure, schema and store)
core-update with an unchanged schema (A4b 2189: same schema keeps store)
core-rollback with an unchanged schema (A4b 2198: same schema keeps store)
cases.recoveryExpectation: The selected node already exists and was created by an EARLIER, unrelated act. Recovery validates it and never rewrites its predecessor or selectedByIntentDigest.
cases.associationEffect: storeGenerationDigest is unchanged, so every existing association keeps joining by binary equality.
cases.selectedTriple: (selectedStoreRoot marker, toStoreGeneration, toStateSchema); the markers must be equal and the triple must equal the current triple.

cases.condition: toStateSchema is LESS than fromStateSchema; the owner requires a different store generation for these operations
ownerAdmittedFixtures: a composed core-rollback (4,2)->(3,1), admitted by the owner before use
cases.physicalStore: the retained predecessor store is re-opened
cases.instanceIdentity: the retained store keeps its ORIGINAL storeInstanceId, read from its unchanged marker; no fresh identity is minted
cases.recoveryExpectation: The re-selected ancestor node already exists with its own origin. Recovery validates it, additionally verifies that it really is an ancestor of the current node (the owner has no lineage knowledge and cannot check this), and never rewrites it.
cases.associationEffect: The active triple becomes byte-identical to the pre-migration triple, so storeGenerationDigest is byte-identical and every association written before the forward transition joins by plain binary equality, with no lineage walk and no row rewrite. Associations in the abandoned forward store keep their own digest and are reached only through the chain or reported unavailable: F35 in the reverse direction.
cases.selectedTriple: (selectedStoreRoot marker of the RETAINED store, toStoreGeneration, toStateSchema); it must lie on the verified chain from the current node. A store at the same numeric pair off that chain never qualifies.

cases.condition: toStateSchema is GREATER than fromStateSchema; the owner requires a different store generation
cases.physicalStore: a new store is materialized and the predecessor is fenced RESTORED per A5
cases.instanceIdentity: freshly allocated for the new store instance
cases.recoveryExpectation: This transition created the node, so recovery MAY reconstruct it from this committed intent plus the two store-root markers. Because the owner forbids a same store here, the reconstructed predecessor can never equal the node itself; recovery refuses rather than writing if it ever would.
cases.associationEffect: Associations already written under the predecessor keep their original digest and are never rewritten. Lookups for them follow the chain or report unavailability.
cases.selectedTriple: (selectedStoreRoot marker of the NEWLY materialised store, toStoreGeneration, toStateSchema); its predecessor is (predecessorStoreRoot, fromStoreGeneration, fromStateSchema) and must already exist as a node. A retained branch at the same numeric pair is a different store and does not occupy this triple.

cases.condition: a different store generation with an unchanged state schema
cases.note: Refused by the owner before the companion sees it. v2 wrongly labelled (5,1)->(4,1) a schema retreat for both rollback kinds; the control now regresses both refusals.

nodeWritingRule.identityNote: Every case resolves its selected node by full triple from the store-root markers. The v3 numeric-pair lookup is withdrawn: see rootCounterexamples RC-4.

abortedAttempts.rule: An attempt that the owner does not settle as committed writes no lineage node, so no node can ever be misread as successful lineage. Only a forward-selection transition creates a node at all.
abortedAttempts.retainedEvidence: The retained evidence of a failed attempt is the owner's own transition journal footprint in state ABORTED (A6), which this companion does not duplicate, rewrite or reinterpret.
abortedAttempts.orphanStore: A store materialized by an aborted attempt is never selected and has no node. A6 already states that the published generation was never selected and the GC census reclaims it.
abortedAttempts.noContradiction: Because nodes are keyed by the admitted triple and created only by a committed forward selection, an aborted attempt leaves nothing that a later lawful attempt could contradict, and a same-store or ancestor-reselect transition leaves nothing at all.

durabilityAndReconciliation.noAtomicityClaimed: This companion does NOT claim that the public journal record and a private node commit atomically. They are separate durable writes and may be observed one-sided.
durabilityAndReconciliation.writeOrder: The journal record reaches COMMITTED durably FIRST; a node is written after, and only in the forward-selection case. A node carrying a transition intentDigest that the owner has not settled as committed is therefore impossible under the rule and is treated as corruption.
durabilityAndReconciliation.derivabilityIsCaseBound: Only a forward selection created a node, so only a forward selection is reconstructible. Its full triple is (selectedStoreRoot marker, toStoreGeneration, toStateSchema) and its predecessor is (predecessorStoreRoot marker, fromStoreGeneration, fromStateSchema), both read from durable owner state plus the two store-root markers. The reconstruction is then admitted by the same admit_node law publication uses, so a missing predecessor, a disagreeing duplicate key or a broken chain refuses and writes nothing.
durabilityAndReconciliation.nonForwardIsNotReconstructible: A same-store or ancestor-reselect transition created no node. Its selected node was created by an EARLIER, unrelated act whose predecessor and origin digest this intent does not carry. Recovery therefore cannot repair a missing node in those cases and must quarantine; fabricating one from the current unrelated intent is exactly the v2 defect.
durabilityAndReconciliation.undeterminedBarrier: If a forward-selection node write returns an UNDETERMINED barrier (A10), the writer refuses every further effect of the operation, reopens under the next fence and reconciles: absent means write the reconstruction, byte-identical means done, any difference means quarantine. It never assumes either the old or the new state.
durabilityAndReconciliation.boundary: A node is written at the existing lifecycle-publication durability boundary named in A10, under the held fence and the exact leaseSet, and never inside a level-4 grant-journal append lock.
durabilityAndReconciliation.markersFirst: Marker observations are classified and validated before any dereference, and their requirement is bound to the owner phase: a settled transition needs a readable target, an unsettled one accepts a stated absence, and an observed but unreadable target always refuses.

recoveryTotality.composition: The companion never decides a journal state itself. It reads the action returned by the frozen recover_transition_journal and acts only where that action settles the transition as committed, which is action RESUME-COMMIT or RELEASE-ONLY with journalStateAfter DONE. Every other action, including BUSY, REFUSE and the owner QUARANTINE, leaves the node set untouched.
recoveryTotality.ownerPrecedenceAtPrepared: At PREPARED the owner decides first and its decision stands: a core operation ABORTs because the published generation was never selected, and a store operation follows the S9 footprint, resuming to DONE only when the old store is fenced RESTORED. The companion then applies the case branch only if the owner settled it as committed. A missing node at PREPARED is never a quarantine and never replaces the owner ABORT.
recoveryTotality.preCommittedInvariant: It is wrong to say no node exists before the owner settles a transition: the currently selected store node and its whole ancestry exist and are expected, and a retained branch at the same numeric generation may also exist lawfully. It is equally wrong to demand the target marker there: at LEASED and PREPARING the target store may not yet have been materialised, and after an abort an unpublished target may already have been reclaimed, so an explicitly stated ABSENT target is the expected observation and no premature node is possible. Where a target IS observable, what must not exist is a NEW node for THIS attempt at ITS OWN FULL TRIPLE, built from the selected marker; For a forward selection, any node at its new selected triple is premature. For a same-store or ancestor re-selection, a pre-existing node is expected and only a claim that this unrelated current transition created it is contradictory; the case-specific contradiction quarantines. A node at a merely equal numeric pair on another branch is a different store and is neither read nor disturbed. No numeric pair and no intent digest is ever scanned.

byOwnerAction.journalStates: any; fence not held, lease set not re-acquired exactly, registry differs, or a PREPARED store operation with no durable footprint
byOwnerAction.companionAction: no-decision; nothing inspected, nothing read, nothing written
byOwnerAction.markerRequirement: none; no marker is consulted at all

byOwnerAction.journalStates: LEASED, PREPARING, PREPARED for a core operation, PREPARED for a store operation whose old store is not fenced RESTORED
byOwnerAction.companionAction: none; only the premature-node check at this attempt own full triple
byOwnerAction.ifViolated: QUARANTINE / MIGRATION.CORRUPT for a premature node only
byOwnerAction.markerRequirement: predecessor marker required; target observation required to be STATED, and an absent target is expected

byOwnerAction.ifViolated: QUARANTINE / MIGRATION.CORRUPT for a premature node only
byOwnerAction.markerRequirement: same as ABORT: an absent target is expected after reclamation

byOwnerAction.journalStates: COMMITTED, and PREPARED for a store operation whose old store is fenced RESTORED
byOwnerAction.forwardSelection: admit_node the reconstruction at the selected full triple; an existing byte-identical node is idempotent, a disagreeing one refuses
byOwnerAction.sameStoreOrAncestorReselect: validate the retained node at its own full triple; absent, duplicated-and-disagreeing, or claiming this transition as origin refuses; an ancestor must additionally lie on the verified chain from the current node
byOwnerAction.markerRequirement: both markers required and readable; an absent target at a settled transition is corruption

byOwnerAction.companionAction: the same case branch as RESUME-COMMIT

recoveryTotality.originsAreStable: In every non-forward case the retained node keeps its original predecessor and selectedByIntentDigest. Recovery validates and never rewrites an origin.
recoveryTotality.executedBy: controls/check_lineage_recovery.py sections C (seven owner-admitted operation cases x six journal states with phase-accurate target observations), D (root v3 regressions), E (composed migrate, rollback, second forward selection with a retained branch), F (damaged and duplicate), G (owner actions that decide nothing), H (phase-sensitive markers), I (idempotent path validation) and J (lineage components).
recoveryTotality.noDecisionActions: BUSY, REFUSE and QUARANTINE make no transition decision, so the companion makes none either: it inspects no node, reads no marker and changes nothing. v3 prose said this but its generic non-settled branch still inspected the node set; law and prose now agree and the behaviour is executed in control section G.
recoveryTotality.phaseSensitiveMarkers: The marker requirement follows the owner phase. See identityAndMarkers.markerContract.phaseSensitivity. Executed in control section H across LEASED, PREPARING and ABORTED with an absent target, an observable target with no node, an unreadable target, a genuinely premature node at the full triple, and a retained branch at an equal numeric pair.

retryTrace.purpose: Shows that a lawful retry of a byte-identical intent produces no contradiction, and that a retry after a committed transition is refused by the owner's own checks.
steps: T0. Current triple (X, 5, 1). Node for (X,5,1) exists with predecessor null.
T1. store-migrate intent I admitted: from (5,1) to (6,2). preconditionGeneration is the observed core generation.
T2. Journal LEASED, PREPARING, PREPARED. A new store instance Y is materialized at (6,2). Crash.

T3. recover_transition_journal at PREPARED: the S9 footprint decides ABORT because the old store is not fenced RESTORED. No node exists for (Y,6,2) because nodes follow COMMITTED. Store Y is unselected; the GC census reclaims it (A6).

T4. Retry. The core generation did not change, so the same 11 intent members reproduce byte-identical intentDigest I. Admission observes currentStoreGeneration 5 and currentStateSchema 1, which still equal the intent's from members, so CURRENT_STORE_MISMATCH and CURRENT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH do not fire and the retry is lawful.
T5. The retry materializes a NEW instance Z at (6,2) and reaches COMMITTED. One node is written: (Z,6,2) with predecessor (X,5,1) and selectedByIntentDigest I.
T6. No contradiction. The node key is the triple, so (Y,6,2) never existed and (Z,6,2) is new. intentDigest I appears once, as evidence, and is not a key.

T7. A second attempt at the same intent I after T5 is refused by the owner, not by this companion: currentStoreGeneration is now 6 and currentStateSchema is 2, so the intent's fromStoreGeneration 5 and fromStateSchema 1 fail TRANSITION.CURRENT_STORE_MISMATCH and TRANSITION.CURRENT_SCHEMA_MISMATCH (A6).

canonicalDigestRecipe.subject: StoreGenerationBindingV1 as already selected in commit-recovery-plan.v1.json#/storeGenerationBindingSchema; this correction does not change its members.
canonicalDigestRecipe.profileSelection: Product profile. Security S2 (A7) assigns everything carrying a schemaVersion to the foundation canonicalizer of identity section 3. The record therefore never enters opensip-metadata-canonical.1.
canonicalDigestRecipe.canonicalizer: docs/coop/design-corrections/foundation/canonical.py canonical(): json.dumps with ensure_ascii=False, sort_keys=True, separators (',',':'), allow_nan=False, UTF-8 encoded.
canonicalDigestRecipe.recipe: storeGenerationDigest = raw SHA-256 over canonical(binding) for the five-member object {schemaVersion, namespaceId, storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema}.
canonicalDigestRecipe.representation: raw-artifact, the representation class identity-model.v3.py digest_field() treats as retained bytes and nothing more.
canonicalDigestRecipe.notAnIdentity: It is not identity(domain, value). That recipe frames its preimage as b'opensip.product.v1\0' + domain + b'\0' + an 8-byte big-endian length + the canonical bytes (A8), while this digest is a bare SHA-256 over the canonical bytes alone. The two are distinct constructions over distinct preimages, so the two domains are separated by construction and a value produced by one is never admitted where the other is required. This mints no H-domain, typed prefix or semantic identity. It is NOT a claim that a collision between the two is mathematically impossible: SHA-256 is finite, and any statement that distinct preimages yield distinct digests rests on the standard collision-resistance assumption, which this design assumes and does not prove. The v2 wording said such a collision cannot occur and is withdrawn.
whatChangesTheDigest: Changing any value, including an integer's value or a string's bytes, changes it.
whatDoesNotChangeTheDigest: The order of object members in the input JSON. canonical() sorts keys, so input key order is not observable in the preimage. The v1 wording that said reordering a member changes every digest was wrong and is withdrawn.
Insignificant input whitespace, because the canonicalizer re-emits with fixed separators.
Whether the input arrived as bytes or as an already-parsed value, provided parse() admitted it.
canonicalDigestRecipe.noSecondSerializer: Member order, string encoding and integer encoding come solely from that one canonicalizer. No module may hand-assemble the preimage.
canonicalDigestRecipe.comparison: namespaceId is compared by binary equality under the no-normalization product profile; no path resolution, case folding or NFC transform is applied at comparison or at digest time.
canonicalDigestRecipe.frozenAtVersion1: Adding or removing a member changes every historical storeGenerationDigest and breaks every retained association join. The record is frozen at version 1. A new member requires StoreGenerationBindingV2 plus an explicitly reviewed retained bridge that preserves the original digests of existing rows.
canonicalDigestRecipe.domainSeparation: Separation is enforced by where each digest is required, not by an impossibility claim. A storeGenerationDigest is only ever compared with another storeGenerationDigest recomputed by this same recipe; no interface accepts it where a framed identity is required, and no interface accepts a framed identity here.

floorsAndAuthority.note: Three distinct acts. The v1 prose collapsed them and wrongly implied that a new store instance never inherits floors, which would have contradicted A5's authorized migration carry-forward. Corrected here.

authorizedTransition.what: An S9 core-update, core-repair, core-rollback, store-migrate or store-rollback under the fence.
authorizedTransition.floors: Unchanged by this companion and governed entirely by A5: a migration COPIES THE FLOORS FORWARD into the new store; a rollback inside the window sets them to the MAXIMUM of both stores; the boot anchor and any pending challenge do not carry; a poisoned floor is never lowered by migration or rollback, and only S4.5 lowers one.
authorizedTransition.instanceIdentity: A forward selection allocates a fresh identity for the newly materialized store; an ancestor reselect keeps the retained store's original identity.
authorizedTransition.authority: Commit authority is not carried by the instance identity in either direction. It is the existing lifecycle and storage law.

freshInstallation.floors: There is no predecessor, so there is nothing to carry forward. Floors start at their installation values.
freshInstallation.instanceIdentity: Freshly allocated; the lineage node has null predecessor and null selectedByIntentDigest.

evidenceRestoreOrPortableAdoption.what: An evidence-bundle restore or portable adoption through crates/storage/src/backup.rs, which the inventory already describes as restoring bounded evidence bundles WITHOUT restoring trust floors or granting local authority.
evidenceRestoreOrPortableAdoption.floors: This act restores no trust floor. It also cannot lower one: A11 records that a restore keeps floors and provides no floor recovery, and only S4.5 lowers a floor.
evidenceRestoreOrPortableAdoption.instanceIdentity: A newly materialized store receives its own fresh identity.
evidenceRestoreOrPortableAdoption.authority: No local commit authority is imported. Imported evidence is revalidated before local adoption and adoption is a fresh locally authorized attempt.
evidenceRestoreOrPortableAdoption.doesNotInvalidate: This rule constrains restore and adoption only. It does not touch, weaken or override A5's authorized migration floor carry-forward.

associationJoinRules.sameTripleJoin: An association row joins the active binding when its storeGenerationDigest equals the digest recomputed from the currently admitted binding for that namespace. Plain binary equality; the only join used on the ordinary path.
associationJoinRules.acrossLineage: When the digests differ, a historical lookup walks predecessor links from the active node by FULL TRIPLE. Each hop must be an admitted node at its exact triple; a node at a merely equal numeric generation on another branch never qualifies as a hop. A missing, duplicated-and-disagreeing or contradictory hop ends the walk and the lookup reports unavailability.
associationJoinRules.neverRewrite: No association row's storeGenerationDigest, receipt, ExecutionId or commitSequence is ever rewritten by a transition, migration, rollback, restore or adoption. A historical receipt stays historically true; a transition changes current selection and availability, never past commitment.
associationJoinRules.neverImportAuthority: Following a hop reports history. It never revives grants, floors or local authority, never makes an abandoned store's row a current commitment, and never substitutes for the receipt, inventory, carrier and operation joins the recovery record already requires.
associationJoinRules.existingCaseCoverage: F27 already refuses a substituted binding target, F35 already routes migration and restore lookups through admitted lineage without rewriting old ids, and F25 already separates retained assurance from current availability. This correction names the lineage those cases refer to; it proposes no new failure case and no change to the generated F00-F37 matrix.
associationJoinRules.currentStandingNote: Current standing: the F00-F37 references in this file record the case inventory at this companion's authoring time and are not relabelled. The current commit-recovery-plan.v1.json holds F00-F53, because the separate carrier correction appended F38-F53. This companion still proposes no failure case and changes no generated section.
associationJoinRules.ancestorSelection: An ancestor re-selection resolves its target from the retained store own marker and then requires that exact triple to lie on the verified chain from the current node. It never guesses globally by numeric pair and never rewrites the retained node origin.

logicalStateSchema.changesBy: an explicit reviewed successor of that owner plus supported-reader admission

physicalCarrierFormat.what: The on-disk format of the grant journal and evidence carriers: DDL version, admitted record types, platform labels, rollover and read-only recovery behaviour.
physicalCarrierFormat.owner: the separate versioned physical carrier work (COV-03 and the separately active carrier task)
physicalCarrierFormat.why: A carrier format version in the binding would change every historical storeGenerationDigest on every carrier migration and break every retained association join.

randomInstanceIdentity.what: storeInstanceId, 32 lowercase hex from 128 bits of OS CSPRNG.
randomInstanceIdentity.changesBy: creation of a new physical store instance only
randomInstanceIdentity.why: It disambiguates separately created or restored stores whose numeric generations coincide, because A4 generations are not monotonic across rollback.

carrierCoauthorJoin.requiredJoin: If the versioned physical carrier work introduces a durable carrier-format identifier, it belongs to that owner's own record and joins this companion by the pair (storeInstanceId, storeGeneration). It must not be added to StoreGenerationBindingV1.
carrierCoauthorJoin.reason: See canonicalDigestRecipe.frozenAtVersion1: adding or removing a member changes every historical digest.
carrierCoauthorJoin.alsoRequired: The carrier work owns whether a given (storeInstanceId, storeGeneration) can still be read after its carrier migrates, and owns read-only recovery over migrated carriers. This companion states only which store instance and generation is selected, never whether its bytes are currently readable.
carrierCoauthorJoin.notClosedHere: COV-03 and the separately active versioned carrier, migration, read-only anchor and additional race cases remain open and are not closed by this correction.

limits: Whole-install-root substitution is not detected. A byte copy of an entire store root, including its instance marker, is indistinguishable locally. This is the same stated, undetected class as the coherent install-root rollback in A9; the marker narrows coincident-generation confusion and adds no tamper detection.
The allocation and restore obligations are enforced on the authorized lifecycle paths. An out-of-band copy that bypasses those paths is in the same undetected class.

S9.2 PROSE omitted the schema/store pair, but the published reference enforces it (A4b). This correction inserts the pair law into S9.2 itself and derives the selection case from the admitted intent alone. If the owner later changes that pair law, every derived case above must be rechecked against it.
This is a proposed owner successor delta. It is not accepted, not frozen, and confers no readiness. Freezing and an independent substantive review on the new bytes remain required.
No executable product code is authored here. Owning modules are named for implementation planning only; none exists.
This correction does not touch the closed CommitRecoveryAssociationV1 schema, the F00-F37 case inventory or either generated section of the implementation plan.

Current standing: the F00-F37 references in this file record the case inventory at this companion's authoring time and are not relabelled. The current commit-recovery-plan.v1.json holds F00-F53, because the separate carrier correction appended F38-F53. This companion still proposes no failure case and changes no generated section.
The companion node and recovery rules are a design reference exercised against the frozen owner functions. They are models: no carrier implementation, no crash test and no qualification.

Only the two rollback operations can retreat a schema, and StateSchema is currently the two-member enum {1, 2}. A wider enum would admit longer chains and multiple distinct ancestors at one schema; the ancestor-reselect branch already refuses an ambiguous match, but that case has no owner-admitted example to exercise today.

Node identity depends on the store-root markers being readable. An unreadable marker refuses rather than guessing, but a marker that is readable and wrong, for example after an out-of-band copy, is in the same stated undetected class as A9.

The companion asserts no global uniqueness of storeGeneration. Two lawful branches may carry the same numeric pair; only instance identity and the verified chain distinguish them, and a lookup that cannot verify a chain reports unavailability rather than guessing.

The target observation is a companion-internal argument, not a public record member. The six-member node schema is unchanged, and no new public schema, member or operation is introduced by this revision.

Whether a target store root is absent or merely unreadable is an observation the implementation must make honestly at the existing S9 footprint boundaries. This design states the three outcomes and their consequences; it does not measure any filesystem.

rootCounterexamples.source: root-counterexamples/ retains all six supplied files unchanged, plus early-abort.observed.json recording my re-run: lineage-recovery-control (v2), repeated-generation (v3), early-abort with the exact copied v4 law (v4).

findings.what: Root AST-extracted the v2 control reconstruct() unchanged and ran it against the owner-admitted frozen intentRepair. It produced a node whose predecessor equalled its own triple, contrary to the no-self and no-cycle rule.
findings.rootCause: v2 published conditionally on the selection case but reconstructed UNCONDITIONALLY from the current transition from/to on COMMITTED and DONE. For a same-store operation from equals to, so the reconstruction named itself.
findings.fix: Recovery now derives the same selection case as publication and only a forward selection may reconstruct. A same-store or ancestor reselect validates the retained node and never writes one. A reconstruction that would name itself is refused rather than written.

findings.what: The v2 node-writing matrix labelled (5,1)->(4,1) a schema retreat for core-rollback and store-rollback. The owner refuses both: TRANSITION.SAME_SCHEMA_KEEPS_STORE and TRANSITION.STORE_ROLLBACK_REQUIRES_SCHEMA_RETREAT.
findings.rootCause: A four-member stand-in was used and described as owner evidence.
findings.fix: Every case is now an owner-admitted eleven-member intent, admitted by the actual frozen admit_transition_intent before use, and both refusals are regressed by the control.

findings.what: The repeated claim that S9.2 publishes no core-rollback store rule was an overstatement.
findings.rootCause: Only the short S9.2 prose omits the pair; the published reference enforces it and the S9 footprint owns reselect.
findings.fix: Claim withdrawn (A4b). A minimal prose statement of the pair law is inserted into S9.2 itself by the current owner patch.

findings.what: Root built a retained old branch (b,4,2) whose origin digest is unrelated, an active root (a,3,1) and a newly selected instance (e,4,2), then ran the owner-admitted intentStoreMigrate through the actual owner recovery. The owner returned ABORT at LEASED and RESUME-COMMIT at COMMITTED; the v3 companion wrongly quarantined both, claiming a premature node and then a disagreeing reconstruction.
findings.rootCause: v3 identified nodes by the numeric (storeGeneration, stateSchema) pair. S9.3 prose itself says such pairs repeat across distinct stores and the primary key is the triple, so the helper contradicted the prose.
findings.fix: Every lookup now uses the full triple built from the selected and predecessor store-root markers. A retained branch at the same numeric pair is a different store: it neither blocks admission nor is read as this attempt node. No global generation uniqueness is invented beyond the owner.

findings.what: Root supplied an empty node set to forward reconstruction. v3 wrote a node whose predecessor did not exist, with refusal None; only the unused whole-set invariants helper reported the broken ancestry afterwards.
findings.rootCause: Predecessor presence, acyclicity and uniqueness were checked in invariants(), which was never on the decision path, and publication and recovery did not share one admission law.
findings.fix: admit_node is the single decision-path law used by publication and recovery: predecessor presence at its exact triple, no self reference, acyclicity after insertion, exactly one lineage root, and primary-key agreement. A refusal writes nothing.

findings.what: For the owner-admitted intentStoreMigrate at LEASED the owner returns ABORT. That phase precedes materialisation of the new store, so its marker cannot exist; v4 markers_refusal nevertheless required selectedStoreRoot in every branch and converted the lawful early abort into QUARANTINE. ABORTED is the same class, because an unpublished target may already have been reclaimed.
findings.rootCause: The marker requirement was unconditional instead of bound to the owner phase and decision.
findings.fix: markers_refusal now takes the settled flag derived from the owner returned action. A settled forward publication or recovery needs both markers; before materialisation an explicitly stated absent target is expected and the owner abort stands with no companion refusal. If a target IS observable its marker is validated before any dereference and a premature node is refused at that FULL triple only, never by scanning numeric pairs or digests. An observed-but-unreadable target still refuses and is never read as absence. BUSY, REFUSE and QUARANTINE remain no-decision and consult no marker at all.

findings.what: admit_node returned idempotent on an exact target match BEFORE running ancestry. Root supplied an existing exact target whose immediate predecessor existed but whose predecessor chain was broken; v4 returned validated with refusal None while the whole-set auditor reported the broken chain.
findings.rootCause: The idempotent short-circuit bypassed the mandatory chain and uniqueness checks, so the decision path and the auditor disagreed.
findings.fix: Chain and uniqueness validation runs on the idempotent path too, over the set that will stand. It still writes nothing and never rewrites an origin. The same validation was added to the non-forward validation path. A clean existing node validates positively; a broken or cyclic one refuses.

lineageRoot.definition: A node whose predecessor and selectedByIntentDigest are both null. It is the start of one store lineage and has no ancestry.
lineageRoot.whyNotTiedToInstallation: v2 admitted the paired nulls only at installation. An authorized evidence restore or portable adoption also materialises a NEW physical store, and it has no admitted S9 transition intent, so it had no lawful node under that rule. Generalising the root to any authorized local act fixes this without inventing a public transition or adding a member.

creatingActs.ancestry: none; this is the first store

creatingActs.act: authorized evidence restore or portable adoption
creatingActs.owner: crates/storage/src/backup.rs, already described in the inventory as restoring bounded evidence bundles without restoring trust floors or granting local authority
creatingActs.ancestry: none is imported from the source store

obligations: The act allocates a FRESH storeInstanceId from 128 bits of OS CSPRNG for the new physical store.

If the materialised bytes contain a store-root marker copied from a source store, the act REPLACES it with the freshly allocated identity before the store is first published. A restored marker must never impersonate the source store.
No node is imported from the source. The new lineage begins at its own root with predecessor null, even when the source had ancestry.
selectedByIntentDigest is null because there is no admitted S9 transition intent. No transition is invented to manufacture one, and no public record gains a member.
No floor, grant or local commit authority is imported. Imported evidence is revalidated before local adoption and adoption is a fresh locally authorized attempt.
lineageRoot.lookupConsequence: A storeGenerationDigest from the source store is simply not in the local chain. A walk terminates at the local root and the lookup reports unavailability. It never reports the source commitment as locally committed.
lineageRoot.whichActCreatedARoot: Recorded by the existing owners, installation.rs and backup.rs, and by their own durable records. This companion does not duplicate that distinction, so the six-member record shape is unchanged.
lineageRoot.detectionLimit: An out-of-band raw copy of a whole store root that bypasses these authorized paths is in the same stated, undetected class as A9.

identityAndMarkers.principle: A node is identified by its FULL TRIPLE (storeInstanceId, storeGeneration, stateSchema) at every decision point. The numeric pair alone never identifies a node, because S9.2 generations are not monotonic and a retained branch can present the same pair as a fresh target.

markerContract.selectedStoreRoot: The storeInstanceId read from the root of the store this transition SELECTS: the newly materialised store for a forward selection, the retained ancestor for a re-selection, the unchanged store for a same-store operation.
markerContract.predecessorStoreRoot: The storeInstanceId read from the root of the store the transition comes from. That store is the currently selected one, so it exists in every phase and is always required whenever the companion decides anything.
markerContract.validatedBeforeDereference: Both observations are classified and validated before any dereference or lookup. Nothing is read, dereferenced or written before that classification.
markerContract.caseConsistency: A same-store operation requires the two markers to be equal; a forward selection requires them to differ. A mismatch refuses.

targetObservationIsThreeWay.readable: A 32-lowercase-hex identity was read from the target store root.
targetObservationIsThreeWay.absent: Stated explicitly. No target store root is present: before materialisation, and after an unpublished target is reclaimed. This is the expected observation at LEASED and PREPARING, and after an abort.
targetObservationIsThreeWay.unreadable: A target was observed but its marker is missing or malformed. This is NOT absence and is never treated as one; it refuses.
targetObservationIsThreeWay.notObserved: No observation supplied at all. Absence must be stated, never inferred from a missing key, so this refuses.

markerContract.phaseSensitivity: The requirement is bound to the owner own decision, not to the companion wish. A SETTLED transition selected store exists by construction, so a readable marker is required; an absent target there is corruption. An UNSETTLED transition (owner ABORT, or RELEASE-ONLY reaching ABORTED) may precede materialisation or follow reclamation, so an absent target is expected, no target triple can be formed, no premature node is possible and the owner abort stands. Where a target IS observable at an unsettled phase, its marker is validated first and a premature node is refused at that FULL triple only. BUSY, REFUSE and QUARANTINE consult no marker at all.

identityAndMarkers.intentDigestIsNotAKey: selectedByIntentDigest is evidence validated ON the selected node, never a search key. The record schema states it may repeat across nodes and retries, so scanning the node set for it would be unsound.
identityAndMarkers.noInventedUniqueness: No global uniqueness of storeGeneration is asserted beyond what the owner already enforces. Two distinct stores may lawfully carry the same numeric pair; only their instance identities distinguish them.

admissionLaw.oneLawBothPaths: Publication and recovery both call admit_node. They cannot diverge, which is the correction for the v3 boundary defect.
checks: Node shape is admitted by the REAL closed schema of this document through the frozen foundation ExactValidator, whose integer type checker refuses a JSON boolean. The law assumes no member set, type or version constant of its own; a caller that already admitted its inputs must state that assumption explicitly, and otherwise the law refuses.
predecessor and selectedByIntentDigest are null together (a lineage root) or present together.
A node never names its own triple as predecessor.
A non-null predecessor must already EXIST as a node at that exact full triple. This is checked on the decision path, not by a later audit.
A duplicate exact primary key whose contents disagree refuses; it never selects the first match.
The chain from the node under consideration is acyclic, every hop is present at its exact triple, every chain member is itself schema-admitted, and the chain terminates at exactly ONE lineage root.
admissionLaw.onRefusal: Nothing is written. The node set returned is the input set unchanged.
admissionLaw.executedBy: controls/check_lineage_recovery.py sections F (damaged and duplicate, including a node failing real schema admission), I (idempotent path: broken chain, clean chain, cyclic chain, and the non-forward dangling chain) and J (component scoping beside a restored lineage).
admissionLaw.idempotentPathValidatesToo: An exact byte-identical match at the target key is idempotent, but it is NOT a short circuit: the same chain and uniqueness validation runs over the set that will stand. It writes nothing and rewrites no origin. v4 returned idempotent before that validation, so a broken existing chain passed with no refusal.
admissionLaw.rootScoping: Exactly one lineage root is a COMPONENT invariant. Several lineages may coexist, for example after an authorized restore or adoption starts its own, so the rule is that the chain from the node under consideration reaches exactly one root, not that the whole node set has one. The whole-set auditor takes an explicit expected component count rather than assuming one.

rootIntegrationClarifications: Unsettled same-store/ancestor nodes are expected: the premature target-existence test applies only to forward selection, matching the case-bound reference helper.
PREPARING can observe a not-yet-materialized target; stated absence and observed readable/unreadable states remain distinct.
Root report-asset provenance restoration is separately integrated; PS01 changes no asset schema.
